text:
Ryan O'Reilly was drafted 33rd overall in 2009 by the very franchise he beat on Saturday, and he made it count: two goals and two assists as Nashville ran Colorado out of Bridgestone Arena, 6-2. Steven Stamkos added two goals of his own, and Filip Forsberg had a goal and two assists. Seven of the eight goals in the game came after a power play or a flurry; Nashville's man advantage went 4 for 7, while Colorado went 0 for 4 and took 21 penalty minutes to Nashville's 15.

Our numbers say the margin flattered Nashville less than you'd think, but not by a lot. Nashville's deserved-to-win figure (the share of simulated replays of every shot that the team wins) was 64 percent, and the first two periods were dead even in expected goals, which measure the quality of chances. Colorado actually led that category after two, 2.14 to 2.11. The game opened up from there: three goals in 1:19 of the second period's last four minutes or so, then a third period in which Nashville out-chanced Colorado 1.14 to 0.30. Scott Wedgewood allowed 2.8 goals more than his 35 shots deserved, while Justus Annunen stopped 19 of 21 and was only slightly better than expected.

Colorado did claw back with Artturi Lehkonen's tip-in and a 5 percent chance Devon Toews converted early in the third, but Stamkos answered on the power play to close it out. Our facts don't include standings or streaks for either side, so we'll leave it there: a night when Nashville's special teams decided things, and Colorado's penalty trouble made every other problem worse.
